whatFailed: POST /v2/bookings/{bookingUid}/request-reschedule, a documented Cal.com API v2 operation, is not routed at all in the Cal.diy build: Nest answered 404 NotFoundException "Cannot POST /v2/bookings/5fT3LTWxLc83LVmjBioSY5/request-reschedule" instead of the documented 200.

docClaim.quote: Request to reschedule a booking. The booking will be cancelled and the attendee will receive an email with a link to reschedule. ... Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. ... paths: /v2/bookings/{bookingUid}/request-reschedule: post: ... operationId: BookingsController_2026_02_25_requestReschedule ... parameters: - name: cal-api-version ... description: Must be set to 2026-02-25. required: true ... responses: '200': ... RequestRescheduleOutput_2024_08_13: type: object properties: status: enum: [success, error] ... required: [status]

observed: Step 1 created booking uid 5fT3LTWxLc83LVmjBioSY5 (201, status accepted). Step 2 POSTed to /v2/bookings/5fT3LTWxLc83LVmjBioSY5/request-reschedule with cal-api-version: 2026-02-25 and body {"rescheduleReason": "..."} and got HTTP 404 with {"status":"error","error":{"code":"NotFoundException","message":"Cannot POST /v2/bookings/5fT3LTWxLc83LVmjBioSY5/request-reschedule"}}. server.stdout.txt shows the request reaching the app (Incoming Request logged, auth fine: the prior call ran as userId 1) and then HttpExceptionFilter emitting Nest's generic unmatched-route NotFoundException. This is a router miss, not a version rejection, not an auth failure, and not a missing booking: the message is Nest's default "Cannot POST <url>" text.
impact: Anyone reading Cal.com's public API v2 reference and driving a Cal.diy / self-hosted build gets a hard 404 on a documented endpoint; the underlying capability (cancel the booking and email the attendee a reschedule link) exists in Cal.diy but is only reachable from the web UI via tRPC, so there is no REST path to automate host-initiated reschedule requests. No data loss, a missing documented contract.

rootCause.explanation: The documented operation has no implementation anywhere in the tested tree. BookingsController_2024_08_13 (the only booking-action controller that ships) declares @Post("/"), @Post("/:bookingUid/reschedule") (296), @Post("/:bookingUid/cancel") (336), @Post("/:bookingUid/mark-absent") (390), @Post("/:bookingUid/reassign") (415/439), @Post("/:bookingUid/confirm") (470) and @Post("/:bookingUid/decline") (494), and no request-reschedule sibling. `git grep request-reschedule` and `git grep requestReschedule` over apps/api/v2 and packages/platform in the tested worktree return nothing at all, so no version of the API exposes it. Two independent things are wrong relative to the doc: (1) the doc mandates cal-api-version 2026-02-25 and names operationId BookingsController_2026_02_25_requestReschedule, but packages/platform/constants/api.ts:56-68 lists only 2024-06-14, 2024-06-11, 2024-04-15, 2024-08-13, 2024-09-04, and apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts:31-41 silently downgrades an unknown header to 2024-04-15 (systemic cause 1); (2) even on the versions Cal.diy does have, the path does not exist, so the header is irrelevant here and the scenario would 404 identically with cal-api-version 2024-08-13 or 2024-04-15. The behavior the doc describes IS implemented in the product: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts sets the booking to BookingStatus.CANCELLED with rescheduled: true and cancellationReason (lines 80-84) and calls sendRequestRescheduleEmailAndSMS (line 206). Only the REST v2 surface is missing. Corroborating first-party record: .github/oasdiff-err-ignore.txt:2022 in the tested tree reads "POST /v2/bookings/{bookingUid}/request-reschedule api path removed without deprecation", one of 180 such path-removal entries (the rest are mostly /v2/organizations/* EE endpoints) that the Cal.diy fork commit added in bulk; the pre-fork parent a17f28e9ab has zero such entries, and the workflow that consumed the file (.github/workflows/check-api-v2-breaking-changes.yml at a17f28e9ab) diffed the fork's generated spec against calcom/cal.com main's published docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json. Caveat: the openapi.json committed at a17f28e9ab itself has no request-reschedule path and no BookingsController_2026_02_25_* operation, so the live baseline that produced the entry was ahead of the committed OSS artifact. Do not lean on the oasdiff line alone; the grep-level absence plus PR #28243 settle it.

introducedBy.title: refactor: Cal.diy
introducedBy.note: Not a regression introduced by a code change to a working route: the endpoint never existed in the public OSS tree. The last pre-fork public spec (git show a17f28e9ab:docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json) lists booking operationIds only up to BookingsController_2024_08_13_* and contains no request-reschedule path. The fork commit ab21c7f805a is the point at which Cal.diy formally recorded the path as absent relative to Cal.com's published spec (.github/oasdiff-err-ignore.txt:2022, git blame). The commercial implementation lives in a BookingsController_2026_02_25 that is not in any public repo, so the introducing change on the Cal.com side is not verifiable from source.

notes: Not a test-defect. The scenario's own step-2 note says the author knew the route was catalogued specOnly and deliberately asserted the documented 200 so the documented-but-unimplemented gap would surface; the request itself is doc-faithful (correct path, correct header value per the doc, the single optional rescheduleReason body field). Answers to the two questions the brief asks for a systemic-cause-1 hit: (a) yes, the scenario would fail identically on the versions Cal.diy does have, because the path is unrouted at every version, so the 2026-02-25 header is incidental here rather than causal; (b) no independent Cal.diy-side defect in the bound claim: the documented behavior (cancel the booking, email the attendee a reschedule link) is correctly implemented in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts, it simply has no REST exposure. Consequences for the rest of the scenario: step 3 (read the booking back and expect status cancelled) would also fail because nothing cancelled it, step 4 (expect 400 for a missing body) would get 404, and step 5 (expect 404 without the bookingUid segment) would pass vacuously since every shape of this path 404s. For the doc author: the page is Cal.com's hosted API v2 reference and carries no note that the operation is unavailable in the open-source or self-hosted build, unlike the plainly EE-gated organizations endpoints; adding an availability note, or Cal.diy publishing its own reduced API v2 reference, would close the gap. For a Cal.diy maintainer: reviving PR #28243 (or reworking it against a supported version) is the whole fix, and the PR body already flags the three review points that presumably stalled it (a TrpcSessionUser vs ApiAuthGuardUser compile-time type mismatch, a status-only response shape unlike confirm/decline, and a redundant booking lookup). Sandbox noise present in the evidence but irrelevant to the verdict: SMTP ECONNREFUSED on ::1:1025 and a Daily/Cal Video api_key ZodError during step 1's booking creation; step 1 still returned 201 and the captured uid was valid.
